program: Bicycle and pedestrian safety policy, education and Denver Streets Partnership
priceScope: Conditional whole annual recipient cost against partial transport-policy health and net resource benefits; not portfolio expected value or a marginal donation offer.

what: Bicycle Colorado advocates for safe bicycling and walking, provides education and houses Denver Streets Partnership within the same legal recipient.
Current legislative priorities describe proposed law and infrastructure changes, not completed construction or measured injuries avoided.
The conditional reference combines finite safety-health benefits with signed commute, participation and public-resource effects.
strengths: Original legal DBA and current annual expenses are verified.
Policy, public infrastructure and education mechanisms are distinguishable.
Separate engaged and downstream populations prevent charging every hypothetical road user advocacy costs.
reservations: Road-user beneficiaries, implementation and incremental attribution remain unmeasured.
Public agencies and other advocates can deliver part of the same safety improvements.
The homepage donation link is currently broken; no validated transaction route or marginal capacity is established.

sections.what: Bicycle Colorado, EIN 84-1201078, includes Denver Streets Partnership as an IRS-listed DBA, not a second charity. Whole annual work includes infrastructure/law advocacy, Share the Road, education and Safe Routes to School. No separate DSP expenses are added.
sections.monitoring: The October2025 priorities explicitly state no target date for implementation. Municipal vehicle-fee permissions, trail funding proposals and traffic-law reforms are intermediate mechanisms, not built facilities, avoided crashes or household disposable gains. Request implemented local projects, agency/coalition roles, before/after injury exposure, county residence and net mode-change costs.
sections.qualitative: The center hypothesizes 5,000 potentially affected statewide road users, .7 Denver share, .4 implementation and .2 incremental recipient contribution. Utility .002 per person-year for three years after two-year delay is an injury-health hypothesis, not a measured program coefficient. Public plans, baseline road funding and other advocates are alternatives; exercise benefits and direct education/event welfare remain unpriced rather than zero.
sections.cost: Full FYending June2025 cost is $1,545,869. Center: 1.534386 health QALYs and .278952 signed income-equivalent years, about $8.52M per better life. A $100 annual net commute/resource gain after tax, benefits, equipment and time costs is judged and halved for positive overlap. Fifty engaged household proxies retain $10 immediate effort costs and stress even if policy fails. Distinct public implementation cost $50,000 and ten displaced-worker households losing $1,000 are judged, incremental-implementation gated. Actual-year effort and delayed resources remain separate; same-year participant gain/cost is joint.
sections.funding: Original full expenses FY2023 $2,089,992, FY2024 $1,785,914 and FY2025 $1,545,869; FY2023 adds $5,460 netted merchandise costs. The $962,129 FY2025 DSP/Share the Road/other program cost is not a narrowly allocated policy budget; all-program $1,282,839 is another recognized-cost sensitivity. Both exclude allocated full social costs. DonationUrl is null because the linked /donate-2/ route returns explicit404 on both hosts; no payment attempted. Fresh restricted marginal use and current capacity require confirmation.

model.costScope: Whole statewide recipient annual cost against partial finite safety-policy channel; direct education/event benefits unknown. Recognized DSP/other and all-program costs are scope sensitivities, not full policy or marginal costs.
model.geographicAttribution: Pinned ten-county Denver CBSA19740. Potential statewide road users and .7 local share are hypotheses; headquarters and DSP branding do not establish county-resident outputs.
model.formula: b=implementation×incremental attribution. Health=(potential road users×b×injury utility×finite delayed duration−engaged participants×current harm)×Denver share. Household resources jointly logged by actual year; full current effort independent of policy benefit, distinct public/worker losses implementation-gated and geography applied once. Price=10C/(health+signed income).
model.counterfactual: Existing transport agency plans, public funding, other coalitions, route choices and baseline road safety absent added recipient advocacy.
model.attribution: Separate .4 implementation and .2 recipient incremental attribution judgments; priorities and legal proposals are not delivered safety outcomes.
model.uncertainty: Unknown traffic exposure, projects/implementation, causal injury utility, mode-change resources, public payer incidence and next-gift capacity.
model.nativeOutcomes: FY2025 original program descriptions and current legislative priorities; no verified annual unique causal policy-beneficiary count.
